justification: SELECT: central randomisation, double blind, 17604 participants, central laboratory hsCRP assay, multiple imputation prespecified with sensitivity analyses. D5 some concerns only because the analysis is a secondary one within a trial powered for MACE; the hsCRP substudy was prespecified, which is why this is not high risk. Industry funded (Novo Nordisk) with employees among authors.

Same parent trial and same reasoning as the hsCRP substudy. Liver enzymes measured at a central laboratory. Baseline values within the normal range, which limits interpretability but is not a bias domain. Industry funded.

Parent trial (Frias 2018) was adequately randomised and double blind, and biomarkers were measured by immunoassay at central laboratories, so D1, D2 and D4 are low. D3 some concerns: analysis required non-missing baseline and at least one post-baseline value, and stored sample availability governed inclusion. D5 HIGH: the authors state plainly that sample sizes were based on the parent trial's primary endpoints rather than prespecified biomarker analyses, and that this was a post hoc analysis without a prepublished protocol. Ten biomarkers were measured and reported selectively in the narrative. All authors are Eli Lilly employees and shareholders. Overall HIGH, driven by D5.

Parent phase 2 trial randomised and double blind. D5 HIGH for the same reason as Wilson: explicitly an exploratory post hoc analysis, no correction for multiple comparisons applied by the authors' own statement, sample size based on parent trial endpoints. D3 some concerns given analysis-set definitions. Five of six authors are Boehringer Ingelheim employees. Overall HIGH.

Same analysis and same reasoning as trial 1404-0002. Reported separately because it is a distinct trial with a different population (normoglycaemic obesity, 46 weeks) and a different weight covariate.

Randomised double blind placebo controlled phase 2a. Liver fat by MRI-PDFF is an objective centrally read outcome, so D4 low. D3 some concerns: the MASLD substudy population is a subset and attrition over 48 weeks is not fully characterised in the available report. D5 some concerns: liver fat was a prespecified endpoint of this substudy, which is better than the post hoc analyses above, but the four dose arms share a single placebo arm of n=19 and selective dose-arm emphasis is possible. Eli Lilly funded.

D2 HIGH: open label design, which for a weight-sensitive biomarker in an active comparator trial permits differential co-intervention. The authors themselves note the open label design as a limitation and report differential use of new antihypertensive and lipid lowering medication between arms. D3 some concerns: 174 of 515 exenatide and 128 of 514 glimepiride patients discontinued, differential attrition, and patients failing glycaemic control exited the study, which the authors note may have selected for responders. D5 some concerns: hsCRP was a secondary endpoint among many cardiovascular risk markers. Note this trial is ACTIVE CONTROLLED and is excluded from Q2 class contrasts regardless of its risk of bias. Amylin and Eli Lilly funded.

Multicentre double blind placebo controlled trial, 171 randomised after an 8 month open label metformin run-in. D1 some concerns: randomisation by drawing of envelopes containing codes prepared by a statistician, allocation concealment not described. D2 low: matched placebo injections, double blind. D3 low: 11 of 171 withdrew (6 per cent), intention to treat with at least one post randomisation measure. D4 some concerns: assay sites and blinding of laboratory staff not stated, and the 12 month SDs are implausibly small against baseline (hsCRP 0.2 and 0.4 against 0.8 mg/l, fasting insulin 0.2 against 42 pmol/l), which is a reporting accuracy concern rather than evidence of bias. D5 some concerns: no registration or protocol cited; inflammation markers named as secondary endpoints in Methods; the authors report hsCRP and TNF-alpha as not different between groups by ANCOVA. No industry funding declared. Overall some concerns; the variance reporting is flagged for the sensitivity analyses.

design: RCT, pilot, biomarkers as stated aim
justification: Single centre 16 week double blind placebo controlled pilot, 23 randomised. D1 some concerns: patients were randomly divided with no method or concealment described. D2 low: matching placebo supplied by the manufacturer, double blind. D3 low: no withdrawals reported, all 23 analysed. D4 low: hsCRP by radioimmunoassay, MCP-1 and PGF2alpha by ELISA, blinded design. D5 some concerns: no registration or protocol; inflammatory and oxidative markers are the stated aim of the pilot but no sample size calculation and multiple markers reported; between group hsCRP result supported by ANCOVA. Eli Lilly supplied drug and an unrestricted grant; authors declare no competing financial interests. Overall some concerns; n = 23 and very low baseline hsCRP (0.4 and 0.6 mg/L) limit the precision of any contrast.

AddHope2 investigator initiated double blind placebo controlled crossover trial, 12 + 12 weeks, protocol published (BMJ Open 2014). D1 low: randomised, protocol published, concealed allocation. D2 low: double blind, matched placebo. D3 high: 13 of 41 randomised did not complete (32 per cent), dropout concentrated during liraglutide (gastrointestinal), ITT uses whatever data were available. D4 low: hsCRP and TNF-alpha by ELISA with reported CVs. D5 high: the authors state that lipoprotein density and low grade inflammation were not predefined outcomes of the AddHope2 trial and describe the analysis as explorative with a risk of false positives; post hoc power analysis only. Novo Nordisk unrestricted grant; several authors with Novo Nordisk ties. Overall high, driven by D3 and D5. Placebo controlled, eligible for Q2.

design: RCT, CRP as secondary laboratory variable
justification: LIPER2 single centre phase IV double blind placebo controlled parallel trial, 24 randomised, EudraCT 2012-005197-63, external monitoring. D1 low: computer generated 1:1 randomisation, blinded dispensing by hospital pharmacy; the CRP baseline imbalance (0.37 against 0.66 mg/dL, P = 0.036) is a chance imbalance in a 24 patient trial, not a randomisation failure. D2 low: double blind, intention to treat with last observation carried forward, 23 of 24 completed. D3 low. D4 low: hospital biochemistry laboratory, blinded. D5 some concerns: CRP is a secondary laboratory variable rather than a registered endpoint; one liraglutide CRP value above 5 mg/dL was excluded as acute infection after unblinding. Novo Nordisk funded and supplied drug; investigators controlled analysis and reporting. Overall some concerns. Listed as Wagner 2019 in Alrasheed 2026.

Randomised double blind placebo controlled crossover trial in type 2 diabetes with albuminuria, 12 weeks per period with a 4 week washout, registered NCT02545738, biomarker analysis prespecified as a sub-study. D1 low. D2 low: matched placebo, double blind. D3 some concerns: 5 of 32 withdrew, all during liraglutide treatment because of gastrointestinal side effects, 27 completers analysed. D4 low: central laboratory assays, log transformed paired analysis, no carryover detected. D5 low: prespecified sub-study with the five biomarkers named in advance. Unrestricted Novo Nordisk grant; several authors hold Novo Nordisk equity. Overall some concerns, driven by D3. Placebo controlled, eligible for Q2; hsCRP was not among the measured biomarkers.
